meta.title: Strip Poker Planner — integrated decision dashboard
meta.trip_window: Nov 17 – Dec 23, 2026 (the dates still open on the official Venetian DeepStack Extravaganza IV calendar)
data_pipeline: data/schedule-snapshot.json — every printed row of the official Venetian schedule PDF, re-parsed each morning by tools/sync_official_sources.py
data/structure-audit.json — every structure sheet the calendar links (37 Venetian sheets + Wynn daily/WPT PDFs), field-matched from the fetched PDF text
data/url-checks.json — last-checked date, HTTP status and content hash of each of the 64 tracked official URLs
data/hotel-facts.json — verbatim sentences about resort fee, room tax, parking and cancellation from the official property pages
data/change-log.json — append-only record of official values that moved between runs
meta.verification_policy: A value appears only when it was read on an official operator page or PDF. Anything not printed there is left blank and flagged. Omission of re-entry/add-on wording is never treated as confirmation of single-entry play.
meta.ranking_policy: Rows are ranked only when the total entry fee, the amount reaching the prize pool and the guarantee are all confirmed from the operator's own structure sheet. The guaranteed-pool ÷ entry-fee figure is descriptive arithmetic about the published numbers, not a forecast, expected value or win rate. Bounty, satellite, seniors, ladies, mixed-game and multi-flight rows are listed separately because their payout shape or entry structure changes the comparison.
meta.no_manual_input: Every table, filter and calculation on this site is filled from the data files; nothing here requires you to type anything to read the findings. The trip calculator is pre-loaded with a worked example and only changes if you choose to adjust it.

walk_policy.rule: A hotel is usable for an 8 AM–close day only if the walk from the lobby to the poker room can be completed inside 30 minutes.
walk_policy.verified_minutes_source: No Strip operator publishes a door-to-door walking time to another property's poker room, so no minute count on this site can be sourced to an official statement. Every walk on the site was instead measured on 2026-11-17 with Google Maps directions in walking mode ('leave now'), from the hotel's published address to the Venetian poker room's published address (3355 Las Vegas Blvd. South), and stored in data/walk-measurements.json with the request timestamp, the distance, the route summary and a link that re-runs the exact route. The official source linked on each row is the page the address came from.
walk_policy.how_to_close: For an official-grade figure: run the same pairs through the Google Maps Distance Matrix API (mode=walking, departure_time=now) with a billed key, or walk the route and time it, and store the duration with the timestamp. Until a property states a walking time itself, these stay labelled as measurements and the ≤30-minute filter stays a measured cut rather than a verified claim.

questions.question: Which of these events actually forbid a second entry?
questions.why_it_matters: The whole brief is 'single entry only'. A $300 buy-in becomes $600, $900 or more if re-entries are unlimited, and the guarantee-to-cost comparison changes completely.
questions.we_have: All 37 official structure sheets for the series, read cover to cover on 2026-11-17: each one prints buy-in, house-fee split, guarantee, chips, level length and the late-registration deadline — and no clause about entries, re-entries, rebuys or add-ons. Two sheets (Valuetown bounty events 18/58) instead say 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200', which positively indicates more than one entry is possible.
questions.missing: A written answer from the Venetian Poker Room (or a rule update on the sheet) stating whether the one-day events are one-entry freezeouts.
questions.how_to_close: Ask the room directly (the poker page lists the contact) and keep the reply as a dated source; until then these rows are labelled 'single-entry unverified' and the toggle filter returns nothing.
questions.owner: you (one e-mail/call) — no agent can produce it

questions.question: What are the exact trip dates, nights and occupancy, and what is the nightly budget and quality floor?
questions.why_it_matters: Hotel rates, cancellation deadlines and 'quality vs cost' are all date- and occupancy-dependent; without them there is no like-for-like comparison and no true nightly cost.
questions.we_have: Mandatory fees that do not depend on dates: $55 + tax resort fee at the Venetian/Palazzo, 13.38% room tax, $20 self-parking / $40 valet per day; $55 + tax at Wynn; $49.95 + tax at Treasure Island.
questions.missing: A dated checkout total (nightly average, fee lines, tax lines) for each candidate hotel on your dates, plus your acceptable nightly ceiling and minimum quality tier.
questions.how_to_close: Price the same dates and occupancy in each official booking flow and paste the itemised totals into the rate log, or authorise a dated-quote step in a follow-up session; until then the calculator uses the advertised starting endpoints and labels them as such.

questions.question: Can a day really start at 8 AM here?
questions.why_it_matters: The brief asks for an all-day schedule beginning at 8 AM.
questions.we_have: Every printed start time on the official calendar: the earliest recurring morning start in the series is 10:10 AM (RaceDay Stack events 3–5, the $1,100 flights and the seniors events); one 9:10 AM turbo satellite exists on Dec 12.
questions.missing: Any official 8:00 AM tournament start on the Strip in this window. None was found on any page checked, so an 8 AM start is not achievable from verified listings.
questions.how_to_close: Either relax the start-time requirement to 'first official flight' (10:10 AM at the Venetian) or name a property whose room opens earlier and have its schedule captured.

questions.question: When does each event actually end?
questions.why_it_matters: 'Primary event + conditional fallback' only works if the earlier event can be finished or exited before the next registration deadline.
questions.we_have: Start time, the printed 'REG CLOSES' deadline for 80 of 93 rows, level count/length and the multi-flight Day-2 restart times from the official schedule and sheets.
questions.missing: Announced finish times — the operator publishes none. Structures with 28 levels at 30 minutes plus six 15-minute breaks describe a 15-hour worst case, so a 5:10 PM entry after an 11:10 AM event is only realistic if you bust out before its own registration closes.
questions.how_to_close: Decide the exit rule (e.g. 'evening event only if bust-out before 4:30 PM') and the schedule page will flag each pair automatically; the underlying math is already wired.

questions.question: How long is the walk from each hotel to each poker room?
questions.why_it_matters: The 30-minute walking rule is a hard filter in the brief; it also decides whether an 8:00 AM-ish start and a late bust-out are survivable.
questions.we_have: Official property addresses and the official statement of where each poker room sits inside its resort (e.g. Venetian poker room on Palazzo level 2, reached from either tower lobby).
questions.missing: Door-to-door walking minutes for every hotel↔venue pair. No property publishes them, and this build environment has no Maps access, so the table is blank by policy, not by oversight.
questions.how_to_close: Approve the maps-API step (S4) or supply the numbers you get from Google/Apple Maps; they land in data/walks.json and the ≤30-min filter switches from 'unverified' to enforced.

questions.question: Which guarantee figures are still safe to compare?
questions.why_it_matters: A guarantee that includes bounties, or one shared across several starting flights, is not the same object as a single-flight cash guarantee.
questions.we_have: Guarantee text for 69 of 93 printed rows, and the sheet-level split of buy-in → house fee vs prize-pool contribution for all 37 sheets. Bounty sheets say explicitly that the guarantee 'consists of the actual prize pool plus the total amount of $50 bounties'.
questions.missing: Nothing blocking — but the ratio column must always be read as arithmetic on published numbers, not as an expectation.
questions.how_to_close: Keep bounty/flight/satellite rows in their own section (already implemented) and re-run the morning sync before any booking decision, since guarantees and start times are subject to change at the venue's discretion.

questions.question: What happens to the hotel rate if the poker-rate qualification is missed?
questions.why_it_matters: The headline poker rate is conditional; the true nightly cost can jump to the prevailing rate mid-stay.
questions.we_have: The official qualification terms: six hours of live cash per night, or a $300+ buy-in per night, completed before 2 AM on the last night; otherwise the nightly rate adjusts to the prevailing rate.
questions.missing: The prevailing rate for your dates — which is the number the fallback actually uses.
questions.how_to_close: Get the dated prevailing rate alongside the poker rate in the same booking session and record both in the rate log; note that the $200 events on the calendar do not qualify for the poker rate at all.

questions.question: Are the non-Venetian rooms still running what the snapshot says they run?
questions.why_it_matters: Wynn, Bellagio, Caesars and ARIA rows come from earlier captures; two of those source URLs are now dead.
questions.we_have: The scheduled monitor re-checks all 64 tracked official URLs every morning and records status + content hash. Today: 62 reachable, 2 dead — the Caesars daily flyer PDF (404) and the Bellagio resort-fee page (404).
questions.missing: A live, dated schedule from those four rooms. Their rows stay in the 'needs re-verification' state and cannot be ranked against the Venetian calendar.
questions.how_to_close: Either accept the Venetian calendar as the trip's spine and treat the others as optional, or authorise a session to pull each room's current flyer/PDF and refresh those rows.

questions.question: Does any Strip room actually forbid a second entry in writing, and will they put it in an e-mail?
questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between the brief's single-entry list being empty and being populated. The published sheets for the Venetian series, the Wynn series and the Bellagio weekend events all permit re-entries; the Wynn daily Friday event is the only one that forbids re-entry while still selling unlimited rebuys and an add-on.
questions.we_have: Read and quoted, 2026-11-17: 37 Venetian structure sheets (0 state single-entry; 13 carry the 'bag for Day 2 then no further flight' rule; sheet 8 prints 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200'); the Wynn WPT booklet (69 event sheets: 67 print 'unlimited re-entry', 2 print a one-entry-plus-one-re-entry cap, including the $10,400 World Championship's 'Four (4) Entries maximum'); the three Bellagio sheets ('buy-in and re-enter through the end of level 8'); and the Caesars page (silent).
questions.missing: A room-written statement that a specific event is freezeout, plus which of those events the room will still be running on the trip dates.
questions.how_to_close: One e-mail or phone call per room (The Venetian 702.414.7657, Wynn 702.770.7654, Bellagio 702.693.7291) asking: for event X on date Y, is a player limited to one entry, and are rebuys or add-ons offered? Quote the answer and its date on the row.
questions.owner: you (one e-mail or call per room) — no agent can produce a room's written answer

suggestions.title: Accept 'structure silent = unverified' as the standing rule
suggestions.problem: Every earlier pass over these sheets produced the same answer: the sheets say nothing about entries, so no event qualifies as verified single-entry.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the single-entry toggle filtering on confirmed rows only (currently zero) and put the operator reply in a dated 'room confirmation' field per event, so one e-mail upgrades the rows instantly instead of a re-audit.
suggestions.decision_needed: Yes — approve the format of the room-confirmation evidence (e-mail/PDF) so it can be attached per event.

suggestions.title: Rank by cost per entry that reaches the prize pool, not by headline buy-in
suggestions.problem: Buy-in comparison hides the fee split: $300 sends $242 to the pool, $200 sends $160, $600 sends $510.
suggestions.proposal: The tournaments table already computes guarantee ÷ per-entry pool contribution for rows whose fee split is confirmed on the sheet; make that the default sort and hide the ratio where the split is unconfirmed.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether multi-flight events should be excluded from that ranking entirely (they pool entries across flights).

suggestions.title: Add a real dated-quote step for hotels
suggestions.problem: No static page can give a checkout total; the rate log currently holds advertised starting endpoints only.
suggestions.proposal: Two options: (a) you paste the three itemised quotes (Venetian, Palazzo, TI) for fixed dates into data/rate-log.csv, or (b) authorise a session to drive each official booking flow for one fixed date pair and store the itemised breakdown with timestamps.
suggestions.decision_needed: Pick (a) or (b), and give the exact dates + occupancy.

suggestions.title: Wire the walking check to a routing API
suggestions.problem: The ≤30-minute rule is currently unverifiable from official pages, so it cannot filter anything.
suggestions.proposal: One scripted pass over hotel↔venue pairs through Google Maps Distance Matrix (mode=walking), writing duration + request timestamp to data/walks.json; the site filter and the day plan then use real minutes.
suggestions.effort: low (needs an API key in repo secrets)
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve adding a Maps API key to the repository secrets and which pairs to measure.

suggestions.title: Let the morning sync drive an 'exit window' alarm
suggestions.problem: Overlaps are flagged as possible, but the real planning question is whether you can leave event A in time for event B.
suggestions.proposal: Extend tools/sync_official_sources.py to publish, per day, the morning event's registration-close deadline and the evening event's start, and surface 'must be out by HH:MM' on the day plan.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the buffer you want (e.g. 20 minutes for walk + rebuy-free re-entry to the cage).

suggestions.title: Decide how far off-venue the hotel shortlist reaches
suggestions.problem: Only the Venetian/Palazzo/TI properties have any fee data confirmed; every other hotel is blank, so 'best hotel' cannot be ranked on cost and quality today.
suggestions.proposal: Either narrow the goal to 'sleep at the host property' (fewest unknowns, zero walk) or nominate 3 candidate hotels so the effort goes into dated quotes for those only.
suggestions.decision_needed: Name the three hotels (or approve host-property-only) and the nightly ceiling.

suggestions.title: Keep change monitoring as values, not bytes
suggestions.problem: Marketing pages re-render constantly; a hash-only monitor would flag everything and hide the things that matter.
suggestions.proposal: The monitor already compares extracted values (start time, guarantee, buy-in, fee split, entry-policy clause) and only marks rows whose official value moved; page-text drift is recorded separately as 'cosmetic'.
suggestions.decision_needed: None — review the change log after a week of runs to confirm the noise level.

suggestions.title: Publish a per-room 'ask list' generated from the gaps
suggestions.problem: The gaps are now specific (fee arithmetic on one Wynn sheet, a stale Bellagio Saturday sheet, Caesars' missing fee split) but they are buried in 252 rows.
suggestions.proposal: Generate the open-questions page directly from the flags that name a source and a field, so each room has a one-screen list of the exact sentences to request, with the quote already drafted.

suggestions.effort: small — the flags already carry the source URL and the missing field

suggestions.problem: Wynn's late registration is printed as 'until the start of level 9', so the site cannot place a second entry after it, and 13 of 38 days lose their fallback (F19).

flags.item: 0 of 93 Venetian rows are confirmed single-entry
flags.detail: All 37 official structure sheets were read on 2026-11-17. None contains a clause confirming one entry, prohibiting re-entries, or prohibiting add-ons. Omission is not confirmation, so no row may be labelled single-entry and the toggle filter returns nothing.

flags.item: Valuetown bounty events (18 on Nov 28, 58 on Dec 19) explicitly contemplate multiple entries
flags.detail: The sheet grants the PokerAtlas PRO $20 rake discount to the initial buy-in only and states 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200' — direct evidence that more than one entry can be purchased, which is the exact spend-advantage structure the brief excludes.

flags.item: Walking minutes are measured, not officially published
flags.detail: Every hotel→Venetian-poker-room walk on the site was measured on 2026-11-17 with Google Maps walking directions from the hotel's published address to 3355 Las Vegas Blvd. South, and each row links the exact route plus the timestamp. No Strip operator publishes a door-to-door walking time to another property's poker room, so the ≤30-minute filter is a hard measured cut rather than a warning — but the minutes are a routing engine's output, not an operator statement. Re-run the route link on any row to check it. Measured: TI 6, Harrah's 6, Caesars 12, Wynn 13, Horseshoe 16, Encore 19, Bellagio 21, ARIA 31 (ARIA is over the 30-minute line and is filtered out of the stay list).

flags.item: No dated hotel quote (checkout total, nightly average, cancellation deadline)

flags.item: 13 multi-flight structure sheets state that a player who bags for Day 2 'may not play a subsequent flight' — the sheet contemplates play in more than one starting flight
flags.detail: Read line by line on 2026-11-17 (session 75757cc1). Sheets #2, #3, #4, #9, #10, #12, #13, #14, #20, #21, #35, #36, #37 (Events 1, 7, 19, 26, 47, 49, 56, 59) contain the sentence 'Any player who bags chips for Day 2 may not play a subsequent flight.' The rule restricts only players who bagged; it does not state an entry count. It therefore neither confirms single entry nor confirms re-entry, and these rows stay 'single-entry unverified'. Full verbatim log: data/75757cc1/structure_reads.tsv.

flags.item: Venetian DSE IV structure sheet 25 (satellites #45/#46/#48) prints an inconsistent blind line at level 25: big blind ante 120,000 with blinds 75,000-125,000
flags.detail: Live re-read of the official sheet (https://www.venetianlasvegas.com/content/dam/vlvweb/casino/poker/deepstack/2026/structures/dse_nov_2026-structure_25.pdf) on 2026-11-17 shows level 25 as '25 | 15 | 120,000 | 75,000-125,000'. Every surrounding level follows the 75k/150k-style progression (26 is 150,000 / 75,000-150,000), so the printed 125,000 big blind conflicts with the 120,000 ante on the same line. Published rows copy the sheet verbatim; no correction is inferred. The satellite structure past level 24 rarely matters (registration closes after level 6), but the sheet itself is internally inconsistent and is flagged for room confirmation.
